hypothesis: Extending multi-scale feature aggregation across three architectural stages—Stage 2 (16x16 resolution, 192 channels), Stage 3 (8x8 resolution, 384 channels), and Stage 4 (4x4 resolution, 768 channels)—will create a 1344-dimensional multi-scale representation that captures fine-grained local textures (Stage 2), mid-level visual parts (Stage 3), and high-level semantics (Stage 4). On low-resolution 32x32 CIFAR-100 images, fine local details are critical for distinguishing subtle sub-classes; providing the linear probe and projection head with access to standardized features across all three depth scales will significantly enhance representation quality.
rationale: In iter 20, concatenating Stage 3 and Stage 4 features (1152-dim) yielded a major leap (+4.20 pts, achieving val_acc 0.6620), proving that single-stage pooling at Stage 4 destroys mid-level visual cues. Incorporating Stage 2 (16x16, 192-dim) extends this multi-scale principle to capture low-level local patterns (textures, fine lines, sharp edges) that are otherwise lost after two downsampling stages, while BatchNorm1d standardizes scale across all 1344 features.
expected_effect: Linear evaluation accuracy will improve beyond 0.6620 by making local, mid-level, and global visual features directly accessible to the linear probe and SSL loss.
change_summary:
1. Upgraded MultiScaleCIFARResNet26 to aggregate Stage 2 (192-dim), Stage 3 (384-dim), and Stage 4 (768-dim) pooled features into a 1344-dimensional multi-scale feature vector (backbone_dim=1344).
2. Adjusted ProjectionHead input dimension from 1152 to 1344 (1344 -> 4096 -> 4096 -> 2048).
3. Retained the top-performing Joint DCL + Barlow Twins loss (tau=0.10, bt_weight=0.5, lambda_param=5e-3) and detail-preserving CIFAR augmentations.
